releases.html:
No migrations. The last fixes from the launch review:

  • Gradiated Cloud training isn't live yet. api.gradiated.com doesn't serve grad's /v1 API until its routing lands, and its bare 404 read like a missing resource. All four SDKs and the CLI now turn a 404 without a problem code from api.gradiated.com into a feature-unavailable error (cloud_training_unavailable, CLI exit 6): "Gradiated Cloud training isn't available yet; run grad local up or point at your server with --base-url or GRADIATED_BASE_URL." The default base URL is unchanged. The README quickstart and grad --help start a server of your own (grad local up, the Docker Hub images, Helm) and say Cloud is coming soon.
  • A run is never billed past its max_cost_usd. The step that carries a run past its cap was billed in full; it is now billed only up to the cap. The stop, the resume check and the run's tokens_processed and cost_usd are unchanged.
  • A transient error while a claimed run or import is built (storage, KMS, a database timeout) requeues the job, spending the attempt, and answers the claim with a 5xx so the worker backs off; it used to fail the job for good. An error about the job itself (its dataset version, labeling eval, starting artifact, source or secret gone) still fails it at once.
  • docs/CLOUD_MODE.md uses placeholder hosts (https://cloud.example.internal) instead of Gradiated's in-cluster Services and routes; the settings and paths grad calls are unchanged.
  • Cloud: a cached API key stops working at its own expires_at, not up to 5 s later.
  • Gradiated Cloud usage export: when billing refuses more than 20 single rows in a tick without naming an event_id (an envelope or contract break, not bad rows), the export stops narrowing, parks nothing, logs an error and backs off like an ingest outage (grad_usage_export_failures_total), instead of parking every row.
  • Gradiated Cloud: the public DELETE /v1/artifacts/{id}/pins/{holder} answers 403 pin_managed_by_cloud for inference: holders (a published model version's pin), so a workspace admin can no longer unpin a live version's artifact and delete it. Only Cloud's internal routes remove those pins; self-hosted servers are unchanged.
  • Cloud: a deleted workspace's purge no longer stalls on a dataset that only evals use. A pass deleted it while a remaining eval (past the pass's 500-row page, or still running) referenced it, so the pass failed on grad_evals_dataset_id_fkey, rolled back and failed the same way every minute; the dataset now waits for its evals like it waits for its runs.
  • An artifact upload whose archive is cut off (EOFError or zlib.error mid-stream) fails at once with invalid_artifact ("upload: the archive is truncated or corrupt"); it used to crash the import worker, retry until max_attempts and fail as "abandoned by its worker".
  • A checkpoint eval that finishes while its run is still training no longer deadlocks the run's progress writes (alpha.5's event-ordering lock took the run's rows in the opposite order from every other run write; Postgres aborted one side with deadlock detected, a 500 the worker retried).
  • grad train --wait | head and other pipes whose reader leaves early no longer panic the CLI with exit code 101; grad ignores the closed pipe and exits as it would have (so grad ... | grep -q still passes under set -o pipefail).
  • The web console no longer renders a blank page in a browser whose locale Intl rejects (Chromium on Linux with LANG unset reports en-US@posix); it falls back to en-US. The Datasets empty state points at grad import FILE --dataset NAME (it named grad datasets import, which only takes Hugging Face datasets), and the Health page says evals run on eval workers.

No migrations. Fixes from the production end-to-end test of alpha.5, Postgres certificate verification and a console Artifacts page:

  • Postgres verify-full. Set PGSSLROOTCERT (Helm: database.caBundle, a ConfigMap or inline PEM, mounted into the API pods and the migrations Job) and every Postgres connection verifies the server certificate and hostname against that bundle whatever ssl* parameters the URL carries (a stale sslmode=no-verify included). For RDS, use the AWS global bundle; see docs/SELF_HOSTING.md "Postgres TLS". An IP-address host is checked against the certificate's IP addresses (node-postgres alone checked it against localhost).
  • Helm: GRAD_WORKER_AUTOSCALING is set only when keda.enabled and an enabled pool takes train jobs (api.workerAutoscaling overrides it), so a queued run without one says "Waiting for a worker (none online)", not "Starting a worker (autoscaling)".
  • Cloud evals before the gateway's eval lane answer 501 inference_unavailable with "Evals aren't available on Gradiated Cloud yet"; recipe.evals on Cloud is always 422 checkpoint_evals_unsupported_on_cloud.
  • Web console: an Artifacts page (/artifacts): every artifact as name@version with its format, base model, provenance, size, age and pins; an artifact's page shows its manifest, provenance and pins, downloads it and deletes it after a confirmation (a pinned one shows the 409 artifact_pinned holders).
  • Artifacts list their pins. Every Artifact (list, get, a run's artifact, import results, the internal resolve and pin responses) carries pins (holder, reason, created_at; [] when unpinned), in all four SDKs.
  • The trainer logs Hugging Face Hub warnings once, as JSON (no raw stderr duplicate).

Upgrading runs migration 0010 (node dist/main.js migrate, or the Helm chart's Job); an alpha.4 database (0001 to 0009) upgrades in place. Breaking and behaviour changes, mostly for operators:

  • Removed settings. USAGE_FLUSH_TOKENS, USAGE_FLUSH_SECONDS, WAITING_FOR_COMPUTE_SECONDS, SOURCE_VERSION_INTERVAL_SECONDS, SOURCE_VERSION_MAX_RECORDS and GRAD_CLOUD_JWT_AUDIENCE are no longer read; their values are fixed at the old defaults (1M tokens / 5 minutes, 30 s, 900 s, 100k, training). The deprecated unprefixed INFERENCE_*/JUDGE_* names are gone too: set GRAD_INFERENCE_*/GRAD_JUDGE_*. The API container no longer gets GRAD_JUDGE_BASE_URL (only eval workers use it).
  • 503 capacity_unavailable is waited out, not failed. An eval whose model has no capacity (a cold serving pool) or whose lane is full (429 past the client's retries) waits in place, honouring Retry-After, for up to GRAD_EVAL_CAPACITY_WAIT_SECONDS (default 720) per call, keeping its lease and spending no attempt. EvalRun.waiting_reason says why (capacity_unavailable | rate_limited | inference_unavailable). An inference outage no longer stores error outputs and zero judge scores.
  • Cloud refuses checkpoint evals. A run with recipe.evals answers 422 checkpoint_evals_unsupported_on_cloud at plan and create, since Cloud serves only published artifacts: evaluate run.artifact after training.
  • Parked usage rows (Cloud). A usage row billing refuses for good (422/409) is parked (grad_usage.parked_code, parked_at) instead of holding back every later row. Parked rows are never deleted and never retried by themselves; docs/CLOUD_MODE.md says how to retry them. Transient failures still retry forever.
  • Rust SDK: datasets().import_hf and artifacts().import_hf are from_hf, as in the other SDKs, and import_hf_with_secret is gone (set ImportSource.secret).
  • JSON request bodies are capped at 32 MiB (was 64), 413 payload_too_large, and a replica handles at most two bodies over 1 MiB at once (the rest wait). The SDKs push 8-16 MiB batches.
  • AUTH_MODE=none checks Host and Origin. A public DNS name in Host is 403 host_not_allowed (DNS rebinding), and a cross-site browser request from an origin outside GRAD_CORS_ORIGINS is 403 cross_site_request. Loopback, IP literals, single-label names (compose services), .local/.internal/.svc names and link navigations still work.
  • Every alert in the chart's PrometheusRule is severity: warning (GradApiErrorRateHigh was critical), and the trainer logs JSON lines on stdout instead of [grad-trainer] text on stderr.

Security

  • Artifact uploads: sparse tar members are refused and a tar holds at most 1,024 entries and 10 GiB uncompressed (a 242-byte upload could write 93 GB). A router, decision or reward bundle's head_file must be the format's own head file, JSON configs are at most 16 MiB, and * in a format pattern no longer crosses /, so sub/model.safetensors is dropped, not kept unchecked. A malformed upload is the tenant's 422 invalid_artifact, not a retried job.
  • Hugging Face imports: at most 1,024 files of the format and one hour; a redirect that leaves http(s) or downgrades https is refused, the token is dropped on any scheme or host change, and proxy variables are ignored. revision must be a branch, tag or commit name.
  • Cloud console and service JWTs whose exp is more than an hour ahead are refused.
  • Web UI: a #key= link never replaces the key of a tab that is already signed in.
  • The TypeScript SDK's errors redact a presigned URL's query, as Rust and Go do.
  • hono 4.13.17 and @hono/node-server 2.1.6 (moderate advisories; none reproduced against grad's routes). The trainer image's build context has a .dockerignore.

Reliability

Chaos round 2; each has a test in server/api/test/chaos-*.test.ts, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Failure modes" has the table.

  • A Postgres connection black-holed by a failover fails within 35 s and is never reused; the SSE hub pings its LISTEN connection. Boot-time migrations no longer hit the 30 s statement timeout.
  • Object storage outages answer 503 storage_unavailable (was 500); long downloads are no longer aborted at 120 s.
  • One failing scheduled source no longer stops every schedule; up to 1,000 sources start per tick.
  • A TokenReview outage no longer expires every Kubernetes worker's lease: a review is good for 15 min while the API server is down, never past the token's exp. A rotated worker token never fails an eval.
  • A GPU worker takes the runs no smaller GPU fits first, so big runs aren't starved. MAX_PREEMPTIONS counts only reclaims in a row that saved no checkpoint, and a reclaimed worker hands back when its grace ends mid-save.
  • An artifact delete or the orphan sweep never removes a bundle a new release of the same bytes references; a pin racing a delete answers 404 (was 500), as does promoting a checkpoint whose blob just expired. A workspace purge no longer stops at its first 500 pinned objects. A restarted trainer removes the job directories a killed one left.
  • A resumed run that ends again has one best and one final checkpoint (it listed two of each).
  • A live event stream (SSE, so wait(onMetric=...) and grad runs watch) no longer skips an event that drew its seq before another of the run's events but committed after it (a run's last metric, typically): a job's events now commit in seq order.

Developer experience

  • Evals on grad local up --dev-models: the stack also starts grad-dev-inference, a CPU OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and points the API's and eval worker's inference and judge URLs at it, so grad eval works with no flags (was 501 inference_unavailable). It serves test/tiny-qwen3, test/tiny-qwen3-teacher, LoRA and merged artifacts trained on them, and test/tiny-judge, a deterministic word-overlap judge. URLs exported in your shell still win. tests/compose/smoke.sh evals the trained artifact with a judge and checks the report in the CLI, the Python SDK and the web UI.
  • scripts/check-docs-snippets.py --local runs the docs' blocks against that stack, and --compile type-checks their TypeScript, Go and Rust blocks (56 were never checked; the README's Rust quickstart didn't compile).
  • TypeScript and Go raise FeatureUnavailableError for any 501, like Python and Rust (it was a ServerError, which reads as "try again later"). TypeScript has artifacts.waitImport(id) and prints a readable plan from console.log(plan); Python's artifacts.download_url is typed ArtifactDownloadUrl.
  • CLI: a run says "Queued", then "Waiting for a worker (none online | N online, all busy)", instead of "Waiting for a GPU (0 workers online)" while a worker is about to claim it. Errors lead with the server's words, grad train sums up the selected checkpoint in one line, and grad artifacts list prints readable sizes. grad local up and down print a few lines, not compose's progress.
  • runs.plan and runs.create warn when only CPU workers are online for a GPU-sized model. A router whose report fold misses max_quality_drop says so.
  • grad local up can sync from a provider on the same machine (GRAD_SOURCES_EGRESS_ALLOW, host.docker.internal).
  • A presigned artifact download is saved as <name>-<version>.grad.tar.gz, not its sha256.
  • Resuming a run you just cancelled says to retry in a few seconds.
  • A test checks that SELF_HOSTING.md and CLOUD_MODE.md list every setting the server and eval workers read, with the code's defaults. The Helm chart sets GRAD_WORKER_AUTOSCALING from keda.enabled.
  • Releases: a registry that rejects an upload no longer holds back the GitHub Release and Homebrew, and a pushed v* tag publishes with no approval step.

Observability

  • One Grafana dashboard, "grad / Training platform" (deploy/grafana/grad.json, also the Helm chart's and grad local up --observability's): overview, queue and scheduling, runs and jobs, workers and GPUs, evals, sources, billing, auth, API and SSE, dependencies and Loki logs. It replaces the Overview, Training and Evals & Sources dashboards.
  • Metrics: grad_http_errors_total{code}, grad_job_failures_total by kind, recipe and error_code, grad_worker_auth_total, grad_token_reviews_total, grad_token_review_duration_seconds, grad_token_reviews_in_flight, grad_auth_cache_lookups_total, grad_billing_checks_total, grad_price_list_age_seconds, grad_eval_inference_errors_total{target,reason} (refused calls count even when an eval stores no output), grad_source_sync_lag_seconds, grad_maintenance_last_tick_timestamp_seconds, grad_usage_parked_rows and the workers' grad_trainer_checkpoints_total. Worker series carry their pool. docs/METRICS.md lists them all.
  • Alerts (metrics.prometheusRule.enabled, all warnings): GradJobFailureRateHigh, GradUsagePushLagging, GradUsageRowsParked, GradTokenReviewSaturated, GradDatabaseErrors, GradStorageErrors, GradMaintenanceStalled, and GradNoWorkersForQueuedJobs for eval workers too. GradApiErrorRateHigh needs more than 0.1 requests/s.
  • Logs: every component writes JSON lines to stdout with time, level, component and the ids that apply (request_id, job_id, run_id, attempt, worker_id, workspace_id); errors carry error_type and stack, and credentials are masked.

Cloud

  • The internal listener (INTERNAL_PORT) starts when either of its route groups is configured: Cloud's routes (AUTH_MODE=cloud) no longer need lease worker auth and an orchestrator key. A group that isn't configured is 404. Helm's api.internalPort serves it on the ClusterIP Service <fullname>-internal (never the Ingress), with networkPolicy.internalIngressFrom.
  • Evals: a 404 from the product's eval-versions call is 422 artifact_not_servable (was a retried 503); the call gets 10 minutes (the product copies the bundle) and retries 5xx. Evals call the gateway with each model's canonical-case id (Qwen/Qwen3-8B); GRAD_EXTRA_MODELS_JSON entries take an optional serving_id.
  • The gradiated source answers 501 source_unavailable ("coming soon") unless GRAD_CLOUD_TRACES_ENABLED=true, instead of failing at sync time.
  • A product-DB failover keeps recently answered API keys working for up to 5 min; the JWKS refresh never blocks a request and a rotated key verifies at once. A replica booted during a price-list outage answers 503 billing_unavailable, not 422 unknown_model, and a heartbeat checks one balance per workspace at a time.

Upgrading runs migrations 0002 to 0009 (node dist/main.js migrate, or the Helm chart's Job). Breaking changes are marked; most affect operators, not SDK code.

Added

  • One artifact registry for trained, uploaded and imported weights. grad artifacts upload PATH --base MODEL uploads an adapter, merged model, encoder or router bundle trained elsewhere; grad artifacts import hf://owner/name[@revision] --base MODEL imports one from the Hugging Face Hub at a pinned commit. An import worker checks the files against docs/ARTIFACT_FORMATS.md and the base model's config.json (a failed check is 422 invalid_artifact naming the file, CLI exit 5) and releases an ordinary name@YYYY-MM-DD-n artifact to download, evaluate or continue training from. Every SDK has artifacts.upload and the Hub import (from_hf / fromHf / FromHF / import_hf).
  • Every artifact has provenance (the run, the uploader key, or the hf:// URI and commit). grad artifacts delete NAME@VERSION (artifact.delete()) deletes one; an artifact Gradiated Cloud has pinned for a model version is never deleted (409 artifact_pinned).
  • Worker authentication modes (GRAD_WORKER_AUTH): static keys (TRAINER_KEYS_JSON, the default), Kubernetes service-account tokens checked with the TokenReview API, or lease tokens an orchestrator mints on INTERNAL_PORT (POST /internal/v1/worker-tokens), bound to a host, job kinds, a GPU size and an expiry. Workers read GRAD_WORKER_TOKEN or GRAD_WORKER_TOKEN_FILE on every request, so tokens rotate without a restart.
  • Gradiated Cloud adapters (docs/CLOUD_MODE.md): AUTH_MODE=cloud (API keys from the product's auth view, console JWTs against its JWKS), BILLING_MODE=cloud (Cloud's price list, balances and usage events), evals through the Gradiated gateway, workspace suspend and delete hooks, artifact pins and resolve for serving, and workspace secrets sealed with AWS KMS (GRAD_SECRETS_KMS_KEY_ID). Self-hosted servers are unchanged.
  • A fair queue. A claim goes to the workspace with the fewest running jobs of its kind, then to that workspace's oldest job, so one workspace's backlog no longer holds up another. A workspace runs at most GRAD_MAX_RUNNING_PER_WORKSPACE_{TRAIN,IMPORT,EVAL} (8) jobs of a kind and queues at most GRAD_MAX_QUEUED_PER_WORKSPACE (500); past that, creating a job answers 429 queue_limit, which every SDK raises at once as QueueLimitError instead of retrying. Workers only get runs whose min_gpu_memory_gb fits their GPU. Runs carry queue_position and queue_message, and the CLI, TUI and web UI say why a run waits ("Queued behind 3 runs", "Waiting for a GPU with ≥46 GB; ...").
  • Usage reports. grad usage prints a period's cost and tokens by kind (training, eval, scoring, labeling, teacher) with the top runs and evals; --by day|week|month|model|recipe|kind groups it and --from/--to set the period. GET /v1/usage/summary, usage.summary(...) in every SDK, and a usage page in the web UI. The old listing is grad usage list.
  • Source controls. Filters are checked per provider (422 source_filter_unsupported or source_filter_invalid) and sent to the provider's API where it supports them. sample_rate, max_records_per_sync and max_records_per_day cap what a source brings in, version_interval (default 15 min) makes a busy source commit fewer dataset versions, and grad sources update (PATCH /v1/sources/{id}) changes any of them from the next sync.
  • Browser clients: GRAD_CORS_ORIGINS allows listed origins on /v1, and grad artifacts download REF --url (GET /v1/artifacts/{id}/download-url) prints a presigned download.
  • A maintenance sweep deletes job blobs no artifact or dataset part references once they are ORPHAN_BLOB_DAYS (7) old.
  • Homebrew: brew install gradiated/tap/grad. The release workflow updates the formula.

Changed

  • The web UI is restyled in the Gradiated brand: dark by default with a light theme, a phase stepper and live indicator on runs, smoothed loss and throughput charts with a hover readout, a cost cap line once spend nears it, and a runs table that fits at 1024 px. Storybook renders every component and page state (pnpm -C server/ui storybook).
  • Evals run on eval workers, not in grad-server. Evals, dataset.score(), router labelling, distillation's teacher answers and checkpoint evals are eval jobs claimed by node dist/main.js worker --kinds eval (the grad-server image; Helm's import pool runs one, and grad local up adds grad-eval-worker). Restarting the API no longer interrupts an eval. Breaking (operators): GRAD_INFERENCE_API_KEY, GRAD_JUDGE_API_KEY and EVAL_CONCURRENCY move to the eval workers, and EVAL_EXECUTOR is gone.
  • Helm defaults to workers.auth=kubernetes: one ServiceAccount per pool and no worker keys (workers.auth=static keeps the generated keys). Training pods run under a low PriorityClass (<release>-training-low), so your own workloads preempt them.
  • Storage is S3-compatible only. Breaking: S3_BUCKET is required, and local-disk mode (STORAGE_DIR, BLOB_SIGNING_SECRET, the /blobs/* routes) is gone. grad local up runs SeaweedFS (S3 on 127.0.0.1:18786) and migrates with a one-shot migrate service. Data in an old local stack's grad-storage volume is not migrated: push datasets again. S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT (Helm storage.s3PublicEndpoint) signs client uploads for another host.
  • grad local up publishes the API and web UI on 127.0.0.1:18787, Grafana on 18788 and Prometheus on 18789 (were 8787, 3000 and 9090). It moves a busy default port to a free one and says so, remembers the choice, and grad local status prints the URLs.
  • Released artifacts live under artifacts/<workspace>/<sha256>, the one prefix serving reads; checkpoints stay under their job. Manifests are format_version 2 (they add provenance); readers accept 1 and 2.
  • Event streams share one reader per API replica (LISTEN on grad_job_events) instead of polling Postgres per stream: with 1,000 streams, about 40 queries a second instead of 2,000, and under 0.1 s from write to client.
  • Import workers upload dataset parts (gzip JSONL, up to 50k records or 64 MB) straight to storage; grad-server never carries the records. Reading a large synced dataset is about ten times faster (180k records: 71 s to 6 s).
  • Source syncs use each API's largest page, fetch traces and scores side by side, and re-read the last hour of feedback for edits every 15 minutes (Phoenix: 7 days) instead of a week every minute. GRAD_SOURCES_<PROVIDER>_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE raises a provider's rate.
  • Breaking: a UsageRecord's kind is the usage kind (training replaces run; evals are eval, scoring, labeling or teacher). Rust client.usage().list takes a UsageQuery.
  • Breaking (Cloud operators only): CLOUD_INTERNAL_API_URL's /auth/verify and billing/usage/cursor calls and USAGE_EXPORT_LAG_SECONDS are gone.
  • The default batch_size is a quarter of the training examples (at least 8) when that is under 128, so a small dataset takes several optimizer steps. runs.plan adds cost_breakdown (training, teacher and eval), and its estimate includes recipe.evals.
  • npm: until 1.0 every release, alpha included, gets the latest dist-tag, so npm i @gradiated/grad installs the newest one (it was stuck on alpha.1).

Removed

  • The deploy surface. grad-server drops the /v1/deployments, /v1/route, /v1/embeddings and /v1/feedback stubs; the SDKs and CLI drop deploy(), deployments, grad deploy and DeployUnavailableError. On Gradiated Cloud you publish an artifact as a model version through the Models API; self-hosted, download it and serve it yourself.
  • The trainer protocol's POST /v1/trainer-jobs/{id}/records: imports upload parts instead.

Fixed

  • Plans estimate what runs bill: each base model's tokenizer density (the dev models' was off by 2.3x), both sides of every DPO and reward pair, and whole batches per epoch.
  • A second run under a queued or running run's name warns in the plan and on create (run.warnings); CLI commands given a shared name pick the newest and say so.
  • grad runs watch and a re-attached grad train --wait show the whole run from its first event, and the empty chart says what the run is waiting for.
  • A Postgres restart, failover or killed backend no longer crashes grad-server: the request answers 503 database_unavailable and the pool drops the dead connection.
  • Concurrent identical pushes and promotes no longer make duplicate versions or releases (migration 0002), and record_count counts a record pushed or synced again once.
  • A retried eval cancel or run resume returns the current state instead of 409, and dataset.score honours Idempotency-Key, so a retry after a lost response starts nothing new.
  • A restarted worker container takes a new, billed attempt instead of its old lease.
  • An eval's or import's final status commits with its bill; a database blip during an eval is retried in place instead of waiting out the lease; an eval worker waiting on the regex sandbox no longer exits mid-eval.
  • Leases follow the database clock on a monotonic clock, so a host clock step no longer requeues healthy jobs.
  • A source sync that fails waits for its in-flight provider requests before returning.
  • Databases created by an earlier release get the usage-report indexes (migration 0009); they had been added to 0001 after it shipped.

Security

  • Kubernetes worker auth only sends JWTs that name audience grad, a mapped service account and a future expiry to TokenReview, at most 8 at a time per replica, so a flood of tokens on the public port can't turn into unbounded Kubernetes API calls.
  • A lease token is bound to its orchestrator and host as well as its lease id, and a replayed /complete answers only the credential that closed the attempt (others get 409 lease_lost).
  • Train and eval dataset streams are served only to the credential holding the job's lease.

Changed

  • npm publishes with trusted publishing (OIDC); this is the first crates.io release of grad-sdk and grad-cli. The Go module tag step accepts a tag pushed by hand.
  • The images are published to Docker Hub as docker.io/gradiated/grad-server and docker.io/gradiated/grad-trainer, with the same tags mirrored on GHCR. grad local up, the embedded compose file and the Helm chart default to Docker Hub.

Security

  • The trainer image installs from hash-pinned locks resolved from PyPI only (CPU torch is pinned to its one wheel on the PyTorch index), with pip install --require-hashes.
  • Source syncs have wall-clock limits: 120 s per provider response however slowly a host sends it, and GRAD_SOURCES_SYNC_MAX_SECONDS (default 3600) per sync.
  • Recipe loggers= (W&B, MLflow) go through the source egress guard: https only, no private or metadata addresses unless GRAD_SOURCES_EGRESS_ALLOW lists them, every redirect hop re-checked and the tracker key never sent to another origin.
  • The egress guard judges the IPv4 address inside NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96) and IPv4-compatible IPv6 addresses, so 64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe can't reach a metadata endpoint.
  • Worker errors shown on runs and imports no longer quote presigned URL query strings or object-storage response bodies.
  • Hugging Face imports accept only Hub ids (no ./.. segments, never a path that exists on the worker) and use the workspace's token or none, never the worker's own Hugging Face login.
  • A job's model id can't name a directory outside GRAD_MODELS_MIRROR.
  • The Python SDK names a downloaded bundle from the artifact's base name only, like the TypeScript and Go SDKs.
  • AUTH_MODE=none refuses a non-loopback HOST unless AUTH_MODE_NONE_ALLOW_REMOTE=true (server/docker-compose.yml sets it; its port is published on loopback only).
  • A regex rubric item that times out runs at most once per eval; the eval's other outputs score it 0 without queueing behind it on the replica's shared regex worker.
  • One API key can hold at most 20 run event or metric streams open per replica (429 too_many_streams).

Changed

  • The Rust SDK is imported as grad (use grad::Client); it is still published as grad-sdk on crates.io, where grad is taken.

  • The eval endpoint settings are GRAD_INFERENCE_BASE_URL, GRAD_INFERENCE_API_KEY, GRAD_JUDGE_BASE_URL and GRAD_JUDGE_API_KEY everywhere (server, compose, Helm, docs). The unprefixed INFERENCE_* / JUDGE_* names still work and log a deprecation warning.

  • A run stopped because the workspace ran out of balance (Cloud) is stopped_balance; stopped_budget means the run's own cap and resumes only with a higher one.

Fixed

  • grad local up and grad local reset only ever write the local profile. They used to overwrite whichever profile --profile or GRADIATED_PROFILE selected, and now refuse when that profile (or local itself) points at a server that isn't on this machine.
  • grad runs inspect --yaml round-trips: zero values (warmup: 0) are kept, a continued-training run names its starting artifact as model, and optimizer, eval_every and loggers are exported, so grad train -f plans the same config.
  • The train/eval split holds out a group whenever the dataset has two or more: small datasets no longer train with an empty eval side (which also made reward-model runs fall back to eval_loss).

First public release.

Added

  • grad-server: datasets, runs, checkpoints, artifacts, evals and API keys on PostgreSQL and S3-compatible storage, described by one OpenAPI 3.1 contract (spec/openapi.yaml).
  • grad-trainer: eight recipes (SFT, DPO, router, decision model, cartridge, embedding, distillation and reward model) with calibrated defaults, cost plans before compute, hard spend caps, checkpoints and resume.
  • SDKs for Python (grad-sdk), TypeScript (@gradiated/grad), Go (github.com/Gradiated/grad/sdks/go) and Rust (grad-sdk), with transports generated from the spec.
  • The grad CLI, including grad local up for a local stack.
  • Public container images on GHCR (grad-server, grad-trainer, grad-trainer:*-gpu), published as main and sha-<7> on every push to main and as X.Y.Z/latest on release. grad local up pulls its own version (or main from a source build); --image-tag picks another.
  • A Helm chart with KEDA scale-to-zero for GPU trainers and air-gapped overrides.

Changed

  • grad is now licensed under MIT (it was Apache-2.0). Every package's license metadata says MIT.
